title: Way of the Sword
tagline: The legendary swordsman who mastered both blade and brush.

scenes.text: Japan, 1604. A wandering swordsman arrives at the Yoshioka school in Kyoto — alone, unkempt, carrying a wooden sword. He has come to challenge the finest school in Japan. The students laugh. They will not laugh for long.

scenes.speaker: Miyamoto Musashi
scenes.text: I have fought sixty duels and not once carried a steel blade. The sword is in the mind. The mind that is disturbed, that fears death, has already lost the moment before the fight begins.

challenge.fact: Musashi arrived late for his duel with Kojiro on Ganryūjima island (1612), having carved a practice sword from a boat oar on the way. He killed Kojiro with one strike — the psychological warfare of his lateness was as devastating as the blow.

scenes.text: Musashi's philosophy — the Way of the Sword, Niten Ichi-ryū — was not merely about fighting. He believed that mastery in any discipline, from swordsmanship to painting to strategy, required the same fundamental principles.

challenge.fact: Musashi never lost a duel in 60+ fights. In his later years he renounced killing, became a painter and sculptor, and wrote The Book of Five Rings — still read by business leaders and martial artists worldwide.

scenes.speaker: Miyamoto Musashi
scenes.text: The Book of Five Rings. Earth, Water, Fire, Wind, Void. Understand these elements in strategy and you will understand how any battle — in war, in business, in the mind — must be fought and won.

challenge.instruction: Miyamoto Musashi: paint each region in its true colour.
challenge.fact: Musashi arrived two hours late — deliberately. The waiting destroyed Kojirō's composure. 'You have already lost,' Musashi said, then charged.

scenes.text: Musashi wrote The Book of Five Rings at age 60, retired to a cave. His strategic principles apply to any contest. Prove your understanding of the Way...

challenge.instruction: Miyamoto Musashi: put the body into orbit.
challenge.fact: Renaissance swordsmanship manuals (fencing treatises) were among the first printed technical manuals, systematizing combat for the first time in European history.

scenes.speaker: Miyamoto Musashi
scenes.text: Kyoto is under Riot. At the end of every round, any side whose Strength totals under 5 is swept from the board. Francesco Borromini is already there and far too weak to last. Put me there and hold.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 4 · Survival. Deploy Miyamoto Musashi to Kyoto, keep at least 5 Strength there, and End Turn until two round endings have passed.
challenge.fact: A Local Survival event is a test, not a fight: at the end of each round every side at the location is checked, and a total under 5 loses every card there to the discard pile. Reinforce with followers, or retrieve a weak card before the round ends.
